public_rationale: The mid-April 2024 production account describes missing controls for matching characters across shots, different outputs from identical prompts and unwanted changes to the balloon character [e1](https://www.fxguide.com/fxfeatured/actually-using-sora). These findings support the contextual claim that the preview workflow could not reliably deliver intended, consistent movie scenes [e1](https://www.fxguide.com/fxfeatured/actually-using-sora). The account published May 8 documents a completed music video using about 55 of roughly 700 generated clips; this shows useful output but does not establish reliable control of intended scenes [e2](https://www.fxguide.com/fxfeatured/1st-sora-music-video-how-sora-is-evolving-guessing-possible-pricing).
limitations: The evidence supports a limitation in reliable scene control, not a literal claim that Sora had no filmmaking use.
The packet provides no matched production test or agreed threshold separating ordinary post-production from substantial corrective work.
The finding concerns the documented April–May 2024 preview workflows, not later versions.

our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading concerns Sora's usefulness for making directed, consistent movie scenes, rather than whether it can produce any usable footage.
Ordinary editing and color grading do not establish failure. Repeatedly changing the intended scene or repairing unwanted content is relevant evidence of a workflow limitation.
The speaker supplies no reporting period. I use the latest completed month and the elapsed publication month, April 1 through May 13, 2024, for the ongoing preview workflow.
The phrase about making a movie specifies the use case; it is not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary production records establish that Sora could not reliably deliver intended, consistent movie scenes without substantial corrective work or changes to the intended scenes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented professional movie production demonstrates that the contemporary Sora workflow reliably delivered intended, consistent scenes with ordinary production work.
